hits.draft_en:
Some of my friends outside Brazil still think São Paulo is an easy trip. Here is the ride that changed how I talk about it.

Instead of flying to Florianopolis we booked a solid Uber driver for the roughly 3 hour drive. Friendly guy. I sat in the back and used the time to work on my Portuguese.

At some point I saw he had no seatbelt on. When I asked about it, his answer was that it lets him pull his gun faster.

Me: desculpa, what gun??

He showed me a holster on his right hip. Since he drives in and out of São Paulo a lot, he carries it for protection.

As the clueless Dutch passenger, I asked if he had ever actually killed anyone. Yes - last year, a man came at him trying to take his car in São Paulo. He is now on trial and being prosecuted over it.

I pushed again: did you need therapy, do you feel bad? He looked confused. If he hadn't done it, the other guy would have killed him. ☠️

Most Europeans simply can't picture the level of violence in São Paulo and Rio. It's outside their mental framework. Brazilians, on the other hand, are blunt and realistic about it.

That's why I avoid São Paulo and spend most of my time in South Brazil. Not European-level safe, yet calm for the most part with little real violence - crime there seems mostly limited to gang conflicts and a few favelas.

I asked locals why South Brazil is so much calmer. The answer most of them nodded along to: cops in the south shoot to kill. In São Paulo and Rio, officers fear prosecution if they do.

It’s been a few months now testing the @maticrobots vacuum cleaner

Before we had a Roborock (essentially a Roomba knockoff)

But the Roborock became kinda useless, it'd always get stuck in any type of cable, it'd always get stuck not being able to get on to the thick rug, so you'd have to prep the room every single time just to use it

Too much work so we just stopped using it

The Matic is, well, completely different. It's not flat or low, it's a chunky tall kinda cute looking cube shaped thing with 2 big wheels

And it's a different philosophy, it has cameras and tries to understand its environment, more like a modern robot or a self driving Tesla than a classic Roomba-type vacuum

That makes it just way way better, it doesn't get stuck in cables, it doesn't get stuck in rugs, it drives and turns around the room almost like a mini car

It's also way more silent than Roborock or Roomba-type vacuums, and measurably way more powerful in both vacuuming and mopping

They also respond very fast to feedback and improve things fast, like companies should be these days (instead of getting stuck in some hellish corporate support flow)

Another thing, I don't trust consumer devices connected to the internet (and nor should you) so of course I asked to Claude to analyze if it was phoning home (remember the other vacuums who upload your house plan to China, that was true). Claude was conclusive, Matic never phoned home anything, excellent

Maybe the best part is, it just looks cute and you wanna anthropomorphize it, and they include 2 googly eye stickers so it becomes even more like a dog/cat/pet

@mehul made a great thing!

outsiders.draft_en:

Their new blog post covers early results and how this fits into Anthropic's broader life sciences ambitions.

This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time.
